_comment: Calendar architecture for single-asset mobile event rental. Two structural decisions drive everything here:
_decision_1_unit_constraint: The constraint is not staff availability, it is THE PHYSICAL UNIT. A service calendar backed by an equipment resource with quantity = unit count is what actually prevents double-booking. See equipment_resources.
_decision_2_no_self_booking: OPERATOR-CONTROLLED BOOKING. The client explicitly requires that customers CANNOT self-book the event date. Leads REQUEST a date; the operator confirms; only then does the deposit invoice go out. Source: seed client, 2026-09-02 - 'we want to own our calendar and not let people do self booking. Is there a way that we can do that and just have the deposit invoice auto send to the customer once we book the date ourselves?' This is a common posture in event rental (the operator is weighing travel, crew and same-day feasibility, which a booking widget cannot judge) so it is the TEMPLATE DEFAULT, not a one-off.

rename._why: Base round-robin calendar; repurposed as the pre-quote consult so inherited workflows stay bound to a live calendar.
rename.status: PENDING - ABC Contractors kept until workflow audit confirms nothing references it; Discovery Call was created new instead

create.name: Discovery Call
create._why: Phone consult before quoting. Qualifies date, venue viability, guest count and package. This IS customer-bookable - it costs the operator 20 minutes and nothing physical, so self-serve is pure upside. It is the only public booking link in the account.

create.name: Venue Site Check
create._why: Optional walkthrough for tight or unusual venues. Booked BY THE OPERATOR when Space Confirmed? is 'Tight / needs review'. The 30-minute buffer is drive time.

create.name: Corporate Consultation
create._why: Corporate buyers have procurement questions - COI, invoicing terms, W-9, multi-date. Longer slot, separate from consumer discovery. Safe to expose because it is also just a conversation.

create.name: EVENT - Unit Booking (INTERNAL)
create._why: THE booking calendar and the source of truth for unit availability. Backed by the equipment resource. Default 4h slot with a 90-minute buffer covering setup, teardown and travel between events. Client tunes duration per package at deployment.
create._critical_service_calendar: Must be created as a SERVICE calendar so a calendar resource can attach. A plain event calendar cannot hold equipment and will silently permit double-booking.
create._critical_internal_only: Do NOT publish this booking link, do NOT embed it on the website, and do NOT put it in any customer-facing email or SMS. The operator books it from inside the CRM after confirming the date. Exposing it defeats the client's stated requirement and lets a stranger take a Saturday in October.
create._deployment_guard: At deployment, verify this calendar's booking widget is unpublished and no funnel step or form redirects to it.

equipment_resources.name: Primary Rental Unit
equipment_resources.description: The physical asset being rented. Quantity must equal the number of units the operator actually owns - this is the hard constraint that prevents booking the same unit twice on one date.
equipment_resources._why: POST /calendars/resources/equipments with calendarIds mapped to the booking calendar. GHL then refuses overlapping bookings once quantity is exhausted. This is the native answer to double-booking and the most important structural decision in the snapshot. It also protects the operator from double-booking THEMSELVES, which is the real risk once self-booking is off.
equipment_resources._constraint: Per the API spec: one equipment can only be mapped to ONE service calendar. Multi-unit operators raise quantity rather than creating multiple resources.
equipment_resources._deployment: Set quantity from the Unit Count custom value. An operator with 2 units sets 2 and can accept two same-day bookings; an operator with 1 cannot.

_booking_flow: 1. Lead submits a date request (form / AI / phone). Tag book-date-requested. NO date is held.
2. Operator checks the EVENT - Unit Booking calendar. Available -> tag book-date-available. Taken -> tag book-date-conflict and, if Event Date Flexible? is not 'Locked in', offer alternates.
3. Operator sends the quote and the agreement.
4. Agreement signed -> deposit invoice fires automatically (the client's explicit ask).
5. Deposit paid -> operator books the event onto EVENT - Unit Booking. The equipment resource now blocks that slot. Tag book-confirmed.

6. Balance reminder fires on the Balance Due Date. Capture is manual - the customer clicks pay, or the operator charges the card on file. This is a real limitation and the copy must not promise otherwise.
_deployment_notes: Assign the owner/crew users to all four calendars - a calendar with no assigned user shows zero availability.

Set availability to the operator's real working hours. Event rental skews heavily to Fri/Sat/Sun and the day can run long; the seed client runs 6am-9pm, 7 days. Set this per client - a weekday 9-5 default hides every slot that matters.
The 90-minute buffer on the booking calendar is deliberately generous. Shrinking it below real setup+teardown+travel is how back-to-back Saturday bookings become a late arrival.
Blackout dates (owner vacation, holidays) are set manually per client.

If the operator DOES want self-booking, flip EVENT - Unit Booking to customer-bookable and publish it - the equipment resource keeps working either way. The internal-only default is the safer starting posture.
